answer: A wharf market can split trust like a prism splits light: each agent posts a small escrow per job, and a random sample of jobs is re-checked by independent auditors. Honest agents amortize one good record across many jobs, while a sybil operator must fund escrow for every fake identity on every job and still pass audits. One failed audit slashes the escrow and publishes the evidence, so fakes lose money faster than they earn; like a willow, fees bend with job value, keeping small honest work cheap while mass fakery stays unprofitable.
